call: A false start is a dead-ball foul, resulting in a five-yard penalty from the succeeding spot.
explanation: Rule 7-1-2 defines a false start as any movement by a player that simulates action at the snap. A.R. 7-1-3 further clarifies that a false start is a dead-ball foul, and the penalty is five yards from the succeeding spot.

call: Foul on Team A for offensive pass interference. The penalty is 10 yards from the previous spot.
explanation: Rule A.R. 7-3-8 addresses offensive pass interference. The receiver pushing off a defender 12 yards downfield constitutes illegal use of hands to gain an advantage. The penalty is 10 yards from the previous spot.

call: Team B foul for defensive pass interference. The penalty is spot foul and a first down.
explanation: Rule 7-3-8-VIII addresses defensive pass interference when the foul occurs beyond the neutral zone. Since the tackle occurred 30 yards past the line of scrimmage, which is beyond 15 yards beyond the neutral zone, the penalty is a spot foul and a first down for Team A.

call: Team B foul for defensive pass interference. Penalty is spot foul and first down.
explanation: The rule states that defensive pass interference occurs when a Team B player illegally contacts an eligible receiver beyond the neutral zone, preventing them from making a catchable pass. Since the contact occurred 8 yards past the line of scrimmage, it falls under this definition. The penalty is a spot foul and a first down for Team A.

call: Foul on the defending team for roughing the holder. The penalty is 15 yards from the previous spot, and the kicking team will have an automatic first down.
explanation: Rule 9-1-16 prohibits defenders from running into or roughing the kicker or holder during a field goal attempt. Driving the holder into the ground constitutes roughing, as it endangers the holder and displaces them from their holding position. The penalty is 15 yards from the previous spot, and it is an automatic first down.

call: Foul on the kicking team for running into the holder. The penalty is 5 yards from the previous spot.
explanation: Rule 9-1-16 addresses fouls involving the kicker or holder. Since the rusher bumped the holder out of position, but did not rough him, it constitutes 'running into' the holder. This is a live-ball foul with a 5-yard penalty.

call: A safety is worth 2 points to the opposing team.
explanation: Rule 8-1-1 outlines the point values for scoring plays in college football. It specifically states that a safety is worth 2 points and is awarded to the opponent.

call: This is a safety. The ball became dead in the possession of a player on their own goal line.
explanation: Rule 8-5-1 defines a safety as occurring when the ball becomes dead in the possession of a player on or behind their own goal line. In this scenario, the defender intercepted the pass and was tackled in his own end zone, fulfilling the criteria for a safety.

call: The ball is spotted at the 35-yard line.
explanation: According to Approved Ruling 7-2-4(b)(2), when a fumble goes out of bounds behind the spot of the fumble, the ball belongs to the fumbling team at the out-of-bounds spot. In this case, the fumble occurred at the 30-yard line, and the ball went out of bounds at the 35-yard line, so the ball is spotted at the 35.

explanation: Rule 6-1-3 states that Team A players are not eligible to touch a free kick, including an onside kick, until it has either been touched by a Team B player, broken the plane of the restraining line and remained beyond it, or touched something beyond the restraining line. This ensures the kicking team cannot unfairly advance the ball on an onside kick.

call: This is an incomplete pass. The receiver did not establish himself inbounds before losing possession and going out of bounds.
explanation: According to Approved Ruling 7-3-4(XI), if a receiver is airborne and contacts the ground out of bounds while going to ground, the pass is incomplete, even if the ball doesn't hit the ground. The key is that the receiver must establish inbounds before losing control of the ball.

call: Foul for targeting and making forcible contact with the crown of the helmet to a defenseless player. The penalty is 15 yards, a first down, and the defender is disqualified for the remainder of the game.
explanation: Rule 9-1-3 prohibits targeting and forcible contact with the crown of the helmet. Since the receiver was defenseless, Rule 9-1-4 applies, confirming the targeting foul. The penalty is 15 yards, a first down, and disqualification for the remainder of the game.
